subject: Mathematics
title: It is Spring!
subtitle: Onam fun: adding and taking away
hero_picture: A happy Onam scene in a Kerala home courtyard: a colourful flower carpet (pookkalam) on the ground, children and a grandmother around it, a swing on a tree, banana leaves ready for a feast.

sections.heading: Picking flowers
text: Onam is coming! Neerav, Niya and Grandma picked flowers.
sections.caption: Picking flowers for Onam
sections.picture: A grandmother, a boy and a girl picking flowers into baskets in a garden: red roses, white jasmine, yellow chrysanthemums, purple globe amaranth.

sections.heading: Adding flowers
sections.caption: Flowers for the pookkalam
sections.picture: Children sorting flowers into separate small heaps on a mat to make a pookkalam: 3 roses and 1 rose, 5 jasmine and 5 jasmine.

sections.heading: Leaves for the feast
text: Neerav laid out 4 leaves. Niya laid out 3.
Everyone sits for the Onam feast.
sections.caption: Banana leaves for the feast
sections.picture: Children laying out green banana leaves in a row for the Onam feast: a boy with 4 leaves and a girl with 3 leaves.

sections.heading: Birds fly away
sections.caption: Birds flying away
sections.picture: A tree with 4 small birds on a branch; 2 of them flying away, 2 left on the branch.

sections.heading: Musical chairs
text: Each time the music stopped, 2 were out.
Take away 2 each time and count who is left.
sections.caption: Musical chairs at Onam
sections.picture: A happy group of children playing musical chairs at an Onam festival in a club ground, chairs in a circle.

rhyme: Cows go moo, one and one make two,
Ducks go quack, two and two make four,
Birds fly away, count once more,
Add and take away, what fun in store!
activity: Take 10 beans. Make two heaps and add them. Then take some away and count what is left.
talk: 4 birds; 2 flew away. How many are left?
summary: '+' means add and '−' means take away; 3 + 1 = 4 and 4 − 2 = 2.

questions.prompt: 4 birds; 2 flew away. How many are left?
Neerav has 4 leaves and Niya has 3. How many in all?
